practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing a meaningful classification for selective execution and CI filtering.

The test performs multiple distinct 'Act' operations (checks numVertices, queries existeAresta, inserts an edge with insereAresta, then removes it with retiraAresta). Decision rule 1: more than one distinct method call being tested -> non-compliant.

The method uses only local variables and does not rely on shared static/instance state or execution order. No @Before/@After are required for this single method; per decision rule 4 this is compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only exercises the happy path (valid constructor and insert/remove sequence). No tests for invalid inputs or exception cases are present and the class contains only this single test method -> non-compliant.
Test only constructs a graph with 1907 vertices and uses that typical value; there are no explicit checks for boundary values (0, negative, max) or edge-case inputs -> non-compliant.
practices_evaluation.original_code:
Grafo g = new Grafo(1907);
Assert.assertEquals("numVertices must match constructor parameter", 1907, g.numVertices());

practices_evaluation.justification: The test contains hard-coded 'magic' values (1907, 1234) and there are no helper methods or constants to eliminate duplication. No private helper methods are used -> non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is short (< 20 lines), linear, and contains no loops or complex conditionals (only a simple if guarding assertions) -> compliant under the decision rules.

The test contains multiple substantive assertions (checks numVertices, existence before/after insertion, non-null removal, and weight equality) verifying several properties of the behavior -> compliant.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations are present on the test method; the test is active and runnable. Although Ignore is imported, it is not used -> compliant.
Class-level Javadoc contains a reference pattern 'REQ-000x', which satisfies the criterion of requirement IDs in Javadoc -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses an explicit timeout annotation (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit timing constraint and counts as a performance-related test per the decision rules -> compliant.
The test method name 'test5' is generic and does not describe scenario or expected outcome. Decision rule 2 marks generic names as non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: There are clear signs of test-generation artifacts (import of org.evosuite.runtime.EvoAssertions and a generic test name 'test5'), which match decision rule 2 for heavy code generation patterns -> non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: No Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming are present; the test appears to be a minimal happy-path check rather than a prioritized, designed scenario -> non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public Grafo APIs (constructor, numVertices, existeAresta, insereAresta, retiraAresta) and does not access private fields or use reflection -> compliant.
Assertions are specific (assertEquals, assertTrue, assertFalse, assertNotNull) and include descriptive messages for failures in several assertions -> compliant under decision rules.
The test includes concise inline comments explaining intent (e.g., 'Initially there should be no self-loop at vertex 0') and contains no commented-out code -> compliant.
No use of random generators, current time, or Thread.sleep is present; the test uses only deterministic operations and local state -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: Although the test creates and inserts an edge, it subsequently removes the edge within the same test, leaving no persistent side effects; no global/static state is modified -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing classification at class level -> compliant.
